title: Saag Aloo
subtitle: Spiced spinach and potato
excerpt: A dry Indian-style side dish of potato chunks cooked with whole spices and then folded through wilted spinach. Quick, satisfying, and as good alongside a curry as it is on its own with flatbread.

recipe.sourceNotes: Saag aloo is a dish of north Indian and Pakistani origin, saag meaning leafy greens in Hindi and Punjabi and aloo meaning potato. The dish uses whatever leafy greens are available: spinach is most common in the British-Indian restaurant version, but mustard greens, fenugreek greens, or a combination are used in the Punjab. It became one of the most popular vegetable side dishes in British-Indian restaurants during the late twentieth century.

recipeTools.notes: Wide pan for the potatoes and spinach.

content.text: The potatoes should be par-boiled first so they are cooked through by the time the spices are fragrant and the spinach is wilted. If you cook raw potato directly in the spice oil you risk burnt spices and undercooked potato. Squeeze as much water from the cooked spinach as you can before adding it to the pan, or the dish will be wet rather than dry.
Par-boil the potato chunks in salted water for 10 minutes until just tender but still holding their shape. Drain and set aside.
Wilt the spinach in a large dry pan over high heat with a splash of water, 2 to 3 minutes. Drain into a colander, cool briefly, then squeeze out as much water as possible. Roughly chop.

Heat the oil in the pan over medium heat. Add the cumin and mustard seeds. Cook for 30 seconds until the mustard seeds pop. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic, ginger, and chilli and cook for 2 minutes. Add the turmeric and coriander and stir for 1 minute.

Add the par-boiled potatoes. Toss to coat and cook over medium-high heat for 5 minutes until the potatoes are heated through and beginning to colour in places. Fold in the spinach and garam masala. Season with salt. Add the lemon juice and serve.
